newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Suspected bomb blast injures two in Lagos.
newsitem.headline: Suspected bomb blast injures two in Lagos.

text.p: Two people were seriously injured on Monday when a suspected bomb went off as the local military administrator was driving along a road in the Nigerian commercial hub of Lagos, police said.

Lagos state police commissioner Abubakar Tsav told the News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) that the explosion happened when the convoy of the military administrator of Lagos state Colonel Muhammed Marwa was passing along the Opebi link road to the state secretariat nearby.
"The administrator was not injured, we thank God," said Tsav, adding that six suspects had been arrested.
He said an explosive device had been placed under a stone.
Last month three people, including the head of airport security, were killed by a car bomb. Police said the victims were agents of the exiled opposition leader Wole Soyinka.
Nigeria, which plunged into political crisis in 1993 when the army annulled a presidential poll that would have restored democracy, has been shaken by a spate of explosions this year.
